chunks: And indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, intends the punishment of all the people of the earth altogether, sparing none of them. Then, when He looks at the elderly moving their feet toward the prayers, and the children learning the Qur'an, He has mercy upon them and delays that from them.

And whoever intends to enter the mosque, let him enter with calmness and dignity, for the mosques are the houses of Allah and the most beloved places to Him; and the most beloved of them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the man who is the first of them to enter and the last of them to leave.

key_terms.الشِّيبِ: the elderly, especially those advanced in age
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an being learned by children
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدَ: the mosques, as places of worship
key_terms.بُيُوتُ اللَّهِ: the houses of Allah, referring to mosques

ai.seo_question: How does attending the mosque and teaching children the Qur'an bring divine mercy?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah’s mercy descends upon people because of acts of worship and devotion, especially the elderly going to salat (prayer) and children learning the Qur'an. It also instructs believers to observe proper etiquette when entering the mosque, since mosques are beloved to Allah and frequenting them is a virtuous act.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.723 - "And indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, intends to bring punishment upon all the people of the earth without exception. But when He looks at the elderly, who move their feet to the prayers and the children learning the Qur'an, He has mercy on them and withholds that punishment”.
